posts.name: Kaivax
posts.cooked:
Our recent adjustments to Guardian have made the Elune’s Chosen build stronger than intended. We’re going to take steps to bring this back in line with realm restarts during scheduled weekly maintenance this week.

Classes

Druid

  • Guardian
    • Thrash direct damage reduced by 25%.
    • Elune’s Favored now heals for 15% of Arcane damage dealt (was 25%).
  • Developers’ Notes: These changes aim to bring this build closer to its expected output: high-damage relative to other tanks, but not abnormally so.

We recognize that the build in question avoids the Apex talent. With this tuning, we’re choosing to not break the Elune’s Chosen build or require the Apex talent. We have further plans to update the Guardian Apex Talent in a future patch to give us more flexibility with it and alleviate some of the current pain points for Druids.

posts.name: Fred
posts.cooked:
Mid-season balancing has started to feel less like actual tuning and more like damage control. Seeing massive 200% buffs followed by sudden 25% nerfs a week later doesn’t create a healthy or exciting meta, it creates instability.

This recent Druid changes are a perfect example of this problem. A build becomes overwhelmingly strong because of exaggerated adjustments, then immediately gets hit with heavy nerfs after going live. That’s not fine-tuning. It feels reactive, rushed, and poorly calibrated from the start.

What makes this even more frustrating is that this is Blizzard. We’re talking about a company with decades of experience balancing classes, specs, and live-service systems. At this point, players expect balance changes to feel measured and intentional, especially during a season when people are investing time into gearing, optimizing, and learning their class.

Nobody expects perfect balance, but players do expect consistency. Right now, the game feels like it’s being balanced with extreme swings instead of careful adjustments, and that makes the entire mid-season experience feel unreliable and honestly a bit amateurish for a studio this experienced.

posts.name: Skruff
posts.cooked:
Why are people so upset about the nerf? They buffed Thrash because some Bears were struggling a bit to get AoE threat in keys. But they overshot the mark a little, so they dialed it back a tiny bit. Overall, Bear damage will drop maybe 15%. Big deal. The problem they wanted to solve is still solved. AoE threat in keys is vastly improved. That’s a good thing.

Now, is the new popular build fun? Well, that’s up to the individual player. As someone who is an older player and a very mediocre player (i.e. I just did my first +10 last night), a simpler rotation is something I’d naturally gravitate toward. I came back to the game for Midnight after a hiatus for many years. I found Awoo’s build and it looked ideal for my style, and I started playing it from launch. I didn’t care that it was 30%-40% less damage than other more complicated builds. And as a player of the simpler build, I freely say that the more complex build SHOULD do a little more damage and SHOULD be a little stronger defensively. Maybe not 40% more but 15% seems reasonable.

Right now, I do exactly what Arahgon says we can do – I have IF macroed to MF and Thrash. I press those two buttons along with Lunar Beam and Incarn when they’re available. It’s a little more of a challenge to find the right time for Sundering Roar, but I’m getting the hang of it. Ironfur isn’t on my bars; Maul isn’t on my bars; Mangle isn’t on my bars. There’s a few other nuanced things, like FR to build the shield before gathering, using SI at the right time, BattleRez, etc. But overall, it’s pretty easy for a mediocre player like me.

The way I see it, the problem isn’t that the Awoo build is too strong, it’s that the Raze/Apex/4pc builds are too weak. And the thing is, Blizzard knows it! They basically admitted in the dev notes that the Apex for Bears just flat out sucks. They’ll work on it and hopefully get us something better in the near future. But for now, this is what we have. I’m hopeful that the complex builds will be competitive in M+ and that the Awoo build remains slightly behind, but also competitive.
